name: Periodic Background Sync
plain: Wakes an installed site every so often to refresh data.
meaning: Lets an installed web app fetch updates on a schedule while closed. The browser, not the site, picks the actual times from engagement and battery.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt; Chrome only allows it for installed PWAs, and the permission follows engagement.
steps: Browser wakes the worker on its own schedule

limits.headline: Can refresh an installed web app now and then while closed, at times the browser picks
limits.user_action: You install the web app and use it often
can: Fetch fresh news, mail or podcasts on a schedule while the app is closed
Wake no more than about once every 12 hours
Update quietly with no pop up
cannot: Run for a site that is not installed
Choose the exact times, since the browser decides from your use and battery
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge on computers and Android, for installed apps only. Firefox, Safari and iPhone do not support it.

story.what_it_is: An installed web app can wake up now and then to refresh its content, even when closed.

marketing.name: Periodic Background Sync
marketing.pitch: Lets installed web apps update themselves regularly in the background, so content is fresh when you open them.

story.for_you: There is no prompt in most cases. If you installed the app, it may refresh news or weather in the background, so it is up to date when you open it. It can use some battery and data.
story.for_makers: Makers get a native feel: fresh content ready at launch. The browser decides when to wake the app, based on how often you use it. It is only for installed apps in Chromium.

use_cases.example: An installed news web app fetches the morning headlines before you wake up, so it opens instantly.
A music web app refreshes your playlists and downloads new songs overnight.
A transit web app updates timetables and delays in the background.
A weather web app refreshes the forecast so it is fresh when you open it.
A mail web app syncs new messages in the background to save time at launch.
A browser game refreshes daily challenges before you open it.
A store web app refreshes deals and wishlists in the background.

history.change: Periodic Background Sync ships for installed PWAs
